items.title: Hebbal Lake tunnel: HC seeks technical presentation amid concerns over water flow
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Thursday, September 3, adjourned to next week the hearing on a PIL challenging the proposed short tunnel project at Hebbal Lake. It also directed the authorities to arrange a technical presentation to show that the project will not affect the lake’s inflow or outflow. A division bench comprising Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru and Justice KS Hemalekha said a presentation by an engineer could address the petitioners’ concern that the project could drain the lake. Appearing for petitioners RK Guruprasad and two others, advocate Sneha Nagaraj said lake land had been diverted for the tunnel project. She argued that the construction would obstruct the lake’s inlet and outlet, and said this was reflected in documents available with the authorities. Advocate General Shashikiran Shetty, however, told the court that the project would not affect the lake’s inflow or outflow. He agreed to arrange a technical presentation by an engineer explaining how the project would ensure that the water body’s flow remains undisturbed. items.title: Picked up for speaking Bengali: Inside Bengaluru’s Operation Mukta
items.summary: What happened during Operation Mukta in Bengaluru and what did the crackdown miss? On August 8, police picked up hundreds of people from migrant settlements across Bengaluru as part of a drive to identify undocumented immigrants. Workers told TNM that police checked their documents, phones, call records and private photographs. Some allege they were detained for hours or assaulted. But there is another story behind the crackdown, the trafficking and exploitation of undocumented Bangladeshi workers who are brought to Bengaluru and pushed into some of the city’s most precarious jobs. Who brings them here? Who profits from their labour? And why are Indian workers from West Bengal and Assam being caught in the same crackdown? TNM ’s Shivani Kava and Anisha Sheth investigate Operation Mukta, migrant workers, trafficking and the politics of who gets labelled an “outsider”. Our new project visits the landscape described in Vande Mataram as it stands today, to ask what has become of the country the national song sings about. Support it here . Bengal’s migrant workers caught between ‘ghuspaithiya’ politics and SIR deletions
